Map objects

The objects on the adventure map that a hero can use, with the numbers from the games' own tables. The names are those of the English and Russian editions.

In Etherlords a hero uses an object from a tile next to it: order the hero to it during the day and the visit happens at night. Visiting costs nothing but the walk. Only the owner of the visiting hero sees the building's message. A "week" is seven days, counted from the start of the mission.

Resources and ether (Etherlords)

Mines are captured by a hero who visits them and then pay their owner every turn. Another player takes a mine the same way. The owner can upgrade a mine twice; the upgrade costs are the same for every player.

MinePays per turn (level 1 / 2 / 3)First upgradeSecond upgrade
Mandrake Garden10 / 12 / 15 Mandrake Root30 Root, 5 Ruby, 5 Diamond, 3 Frozen Flames60 Root, 5 Emerald, 5 Sapphire, 5 Frozen Flames
Lotus Garden10 / 12 / 15 Black Lotus25 Root, 7 Emerald, 7 Sapphire, 2 Frozen Flames50 Root, 7 Ruby, 7 Diamond, 4 Frozen Flames
Ruby Mine6 / 8 / 10 Bloody Ruby20 Root, 20 Lotus, 20 Ruby, 5 Frozen Flames40 Ruby, 15 Emerald, 15 Diamond, 10 Frozen Flames
Emerald Mine6 / 8 / 10 Poison Emerald20 Root, 20 Lotus, 20 Emerald, 5 Frozen Flames40 Emerald, 15 Ruby, 15 Sapphire, 10 Frozen Flames
Sapphire Mine6 / 8 / 10 Star Sapphire20 Root, 20 Lotus, 20 Sapphire, 5 Frozen Flames40 Sapphire, 15 Emerald, 15 Diamond, 10 Frozen Flames
Diamond Mine6 / 8 / 10 Smoke Diamond20 Root, 20 Lotus, 20 Diamond, 5 Frozen Flames40 Diamond, 15 Ruby, 15 Sapphire, 10 Frozen Flames
Fire Glacier2 / 3 / 4 Frozen Flames25 each of Ruby, Emerald, Sapphire and Diamond50 each of Ruby, Emerald, Sapphire and Diamond

Ether nodes (Red, Green, Blue and Black Ether node) are captured the same way. A node gives its owner 30 ether per turn when it has the owner's colour and 15 when it has another colour. They cannot be upgraded. Ether pays the upkeep of heroes and the global spells.

Resource piles of one resource lie on the map. A hero who takes one gets the whole pile once and the pile is gone. Each map sets the amount of every pile.

Shops (Etherlords)

Shops come in three kinds and three ranks. A hero who opens a shop captures it for his player. The owner can upgrade it twice; the cost depends on the owner's colour, and "your gem" below is the gem of that colour: Ruby for red, Emerald for green, Sapphire for blue and Diamond for black.

ShopSellsFirst upgradeSecond upgrade
Apprentice's LabCommon sorceries and enchantments15 Root, 40 Lotus, 3 of your gem, 2 Frozen Flames15 of your gem, 10 + 10 other gems, 6 Frozen Flames
Sorcerer's LabRare sorceries and enchantments25 Root, 50 Lotus, 6 of your gem, 4 Frozen Flames20 of your gem, 15 + 15 other gems, 9 Frozen Flames
Wizard's LabUnique sorceries and enchantments35 Root, 70 Lotus, 9 of your gem, 6 Frozen Flames30 of your gem, 25 + 25 other gems, 15 Frozen Flames
Summoner's HutCommon creatures30 Root, 10 Lotus, 5 of your gem, 1 Frozen Flames20 of your gem, 10 + 10 other gems, 5 Frozen Flames
Summoner's TowerRare creatures40 Root, 20 Lotus, 7 of your gem, 3 Frozen Flames25 of your gem, 15 + 15 other gems, 8 Frozen Flames
Summoner's GuildUnique creatures60 Root, 30 Lotus, 10 of your gem, 5 Frozen Flames40 of your gem, 25 + 25 other gems, 12 Frozen Flames
Stone PortalRunes, cheapest for common spells25 Root, 25 Lotus, 5 of your gem, 3 Frozen Flames30 of your gem, 10 + 10 other gems, 5 Frozen Flames
Granite PortalRunes, cheapest for rare spells30 Root, 30 Lotus, 10 of your gem, 5 Frozen Flames40 of your gem, 15 + 15 other gems, 10 Frozen Flames
Obsidian PortalRunes, cheapest for unique spells50 Root, 50 Lotus, 15 of your gem, 10 Frozen Flames50 of your gem, 25 + 25 other gems, 15 Frozen Flames
  • Labs and summoner's buildings sell only spells of the hero's colour, from the list the map gives the shop. That list has three tiers: an unupgraded shop sells the first, each upgrade adds the next. A bought spell takes a place in the spell book. The price is the spell's cost; for every copy of that spell already in the book it rises: ×2 for the second copy, ×3, ×5, ×10, ×20 and so on.
  • Portals sell runes for the spells in the hero's book (cantrips need none). A rune costs the spell's rune price times a factor: in a Stone Portal ×1 for common, ×5 for rare and ×25 for unique spells; in a Granite Portal ×2, ×1 and ×5; in an Obsidian Portal ×4, ×2 and ×1. An upgraded portal sells 15% cheaper, and 40% cheaper after the second upgrade.
  • The Bargain skill lowers both kinds of prices. See Heroes and levels and Runes and artifacts.

Learning and strength (Etherlords)

ObjectWhat a visit givesHow often
TeacherHalf of the total experience the next level needs (table below)Once per hero
Mentor100 experienceOnce per hero
MasterLearns a skill or raises it one rank: the skill the map sets, otherwise a random one. A skill already at its highest rank is not raised, and a hero with five skills learns no sixthOnce per hero, even when nothing was learnt
Training CampThe hero leaves the map and gains 50 experience every day until he is ordered out; he then returns to the tile he entered from. One hero at a timeWhile he stays
Spring of LifeHealth +¼ of the hero's health, until the end of the weekOnce per hero per week
Spring of MovementMovement and sight +¼ of the hero's movement, until the end of the weekOnce per hero per week

The amounts of the Teacher and the Mentor are before the Learning skill, which adds 25, 50 or 100% to them. Experience stops at level 20.

Buildings to hold (Etherlords)

These are captured by a visit and help their owner while he holds them. Any other player takes them by visiting.

BuildingEffect while held
AltarEther income +25% for each Altar (of the income from nodes and the castle, rounded down)
Healer's CitadelHealth of all your heroes +10% for each citadel
Wanderer's CitadelMovement and sight of all your heroes +10% for each citadel

A Fort holds one hero. The hero who enters captures it and guards the area within three tiles: an enemy who walks into it is stopped for a battle. The owner can upgrade a fort twice: 25 Ruby, 25 Diamond and 10 Frozen Flames, then 25 Emerald, 40 Sapphire and 15 Frozen Flames. In an upgraded fort the hero in it fights with a fully charged Rod of Defense; in a fully upgraded fort the hero's level in battle is also one higher. Many maps place their forts already upgraded.

Gnomes and wagons (Etherlords)

ObjectWhat a visit givesHow often
Trader's WagonThree random resources, 6 to 36 of each (6 × 1 to 6); the same resource can come twiceOnce; the wagon leaves the map
Magician's Wagon3 runes for every spell in the hero's book (not cantrips)Once; the wagon leaves the map
Gnome-MerchantOne random resource, 6 to 36Once a week, for the first visitor of any player
Gnome-Alchemist1 rune for every spell in the hero's book (not cantrips)Once a week, for the first visitor of any player
Gnome-ArtificerShows its message that artifacts are recharged, but changes no artifact, as in the original gameOnce a week, for the first visitor of any player

Artifacts carried by a hero of Etherlords start every battle fully charged anyway.

Lairs and guards (Etherlords)

LairHolds
DungeonOne creature of level 2 to 4
LabyrinthOne creature of level 5 to 7
CryptOne creature of level 8 to 10

A hero who enters a lair fights the creature inside. Each week an empty lair gets a new creature, drawn at random from all neutral creatures of its levels at the chosen difficulty. Neutral creatures standing on the map guard the area within two tiles: a hero who walks into it is stopped for a battle.

Finds, keys and story objects (Etherlords)

  • Artifacts lying on the map are taken by a visit and belong to that hero. See Runes and artifacts.
  • A Global spell scroll lets its finder's player cast a global spell from the castle: the first spell on the scroll that is colourless or of the player's colour. A Global spell part offers Clock of the Apocalypse, Terminal Discharge, Ether Calm and Ether Leak, one for each colour; three parts held by the same hero complete the spell of the player's colour; parts held by different heroes never do. Scrolls stay with the hero and are lost with him.
  • A Prison frees the hero inside, who joins the visitor's player on the cage's tile. Once.
  • A Warding Stone gives the visiting hero its key and leaves the map; if the hero falls, the stone returns. A Rune Stone or Greater Rune Stone opens for a hero carrying its key; some keys open and close it again.
  • An Observation Point shows its visitor's player the land around every Observation Device that belongs to it. It can be used again and again.
  • The Altars of War of the Wild Wasteland can be destroyed by a visit, once each; every one destroyed makes the Fire Konung one step weaker (IV, III, II, I).
  • The Town Center of the Lost City gives the key to the Temple of Time and wins the chapter. In the chapters of the Temple of Time, rocks bar the way to it until the rival's castle is destroyed, and a hero who reaches the temple wins.

Etherlords II

In Etherlords II using a building takes 2 of the hero's travel points for the day (a hero has 8); reading a sign is free. Most effects are given only to the hero who used the building.

ObjectWhat it does
Mandrake Garden, Ruby Mine, Fire GlacierCaptured by a visit; pays its owner every day for ten days and is then exhausted. The map sets the total
Resource pilesTaken once: usually 10, 20 or 40 Plants, 3, 6 or 12 Stones, or 2, 4 or 8 Frozen Flames, by size
Labs and summoner's buildingsThe six shops of the first game's names, where heroes buy and sell spells. See About spells
FortHolds one hero or creature. A garrison of an upgraded fort fights with a fully charged Rod of Defense; in a fully upgraded fort its specialisation level is one higher. Forts cannot be upgraded in Etherlords II
BeaconFor heroes of its colour: doubles the distance a hero can sail each day for 10 days (at most 16 points). A new beacon replaces the earlier one
Ether Node of Synthesis, Ordering, Life or ChaosRestores all the experience a hero lost in the Pale lands, for a hero of a player of the node's colour
Shrine of KnowledgeGives the specialisation the map sets. Once per mission for all heroes; the use is spent even if the hero already had it
PrisonFrees the prisoner, once; the cage leaves the map
Sign, Stone SignShow their text
Magic FontShows the land around the Ocularis Orbs that belong to it. Can be used again
Rune Stone, Warding StoneAs in Etherlords: the stone gives a key, the barrier opens for its holder
Artifact RechargerRecharges all the hero's artifacts; needs at least one artifact, and has no waiting time
Artifact RecipeShows how to make an artifact
JettyTakes the hero on board a ship or puts him ashore
TeleporterMoves the hero to a linked receiver (one at random if there are several)
TunnelMoves the hero to another mouth of the same tunnel. A creature may wait inside; it must be beaten first, and the victory clears every mouth of that tunnel
CorpseSearched by the main hero; what it holds depends on the chapter

Battleground buildings change battles. There are three kinds:

  • Activated for 10 days: the effect goes with the hero for 10 days, and the building can then be used by nobody for 10 days. Reality Convertor, Mech Worms Production Facility, Temple of Frost Wind, Source of Oblivion, Ticks Breeding Grounds, Shrine of Nature, Wolves dens, Stone plate.
  • Activated once per hero: the effect stays with the hero. Magneto, Purify Station, Contagious Fingus, Hermit's Hut, Altar of Storms, Rat Holes, Lightning Generator.
  • Working by distance, without a visit: they affect the battles of every hero or creature within 10 tiles of them. Disturbance Generator, Data Flow, Gravity Anomaly Site, Ether Stir, Monument of Peace, Aviak's Sacred Place, Ancestral Tomb, Resonating caves, Balance Grounds, Protector of Life, Toxic Wastes, Cursed Spring, Active Volcano, Shaking grounds, Links of Pain.

Each building's tooltip on the map describes its battle effect.
